checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in that window: falls, ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and any readmissions.

Falls and near-falls review: count, circumstances, injuries, and whether fall-risk assessment was done. Relevant given osteoporosis, chronic knee osteoarthritis, chronic low back pain, and hydrocodone use.

Fracture screen: any new fractures or injury imaging in the window, and whether osteoporosis treatment is being followed (alendronic acid started 2026-01-28; check adherence, administration instructions, and any GI or dental complaints).

Medication reconciliation: confirm the list against what the participant actually takes. Note starts and stops since last review, specifically hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg (started 2026-01-28, paired with metoprolol for hypertension and ischemic heart disease) and alendronic acid.

Blood pressure trend: review all readings in the window for hypertension control, orthostatic readings if recorded, and any dizziness or lightheadedness, given the combination of metoprolol and a thiazide diuretic.
Electrolytes and renal function: check whether labs were drawn after the thiazide start (e.g., sodium, potassium, creatinine), and flag any results or missing monitoring for team review.
Cardiac symptoms: chest pain or angina episodes, nitroglycerin spray use frequency, dyspnea, edema, and any cardiology visits in the window, given ischemic heart disease.

Pain and opioid review: pain scores, function-related pain goals, hydrocodone/acetaminophen use pattern and refill dates, acetaminophen total daily dose, sedation or constipation complaints, and any pain-related ED visits.
Weight and BMI trend: obesity is documented, so review weight over the window and compare to prior values; note any unintended change. Check knee and back pain effect on mobility and activity.
Function and ADLs/IADLs: changes in bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, ambulation and assistive device use, medication management, and meal preparation. Review any therapy referrals and status.

Cognition, mood, and sleep: screen for changes in cognition, depressive symptoms, and social withdrawal, given chronic pain and multiple chronic conditions. Note any formal screen results or due dates.
Chronic sinusitis, dental, and nutrition: check for sinus flares, antibiotic or steroid courses, and new dental issues (loss of teeth documented 2024), and whether these affect eating or nutrition.
Caregiver and social situation: changes in living situation, caregiver availability or strain, transportation, and any safety concerns. Confirm contact details and emergency contacts are current.

Care-plan items due: review care-plan goals, assessments and reassessments due in or near the window, advance directive and code status status, allergy record (currently listed only as 'allergic disposition' with no reaction recorded; clarify), and any outstanding referrals or follow-ups. Summarize what changed and list items for the IDT to discuss, without making treatment recommendations.
